screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of aminophylline (a theophylline analogue) in 46 patients with acute ischemic stroke. Assessed neurological outcomes and mortality. Fulfills criteria: randomised, population with acute ischaemic stroke, theophylline analogue vs placebo, treatment started within one week.

Double-blind, controlled trial comparing intravenous aminophylline with placebo in 79 patients with acute cerebral infarction. Reports neurological outcomes. Meets criteria: randomised (implied by controlled/double-blind design), population with acute ischaemic stroke, theophylline analogue vs placebo, treatment started within one week.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation study with no control or placebo group. Does not meet requirement for a randomised trial comparing theophylline/analogue against placebo or control.

The study investigates vincamin, not theophylline or its analogues; the aminophylline arm is only a comparator and the trial is not designed to evaluate a theophylline analogue for stroke. Participants are not described as having acute ischaemic stroke.

Randomised, double-blind, cross-over trial of caffeine (a methylxanthine analogue) versus placebo in 19 patients recovering from acute ischaemic stroke. Meets criteria: randomised design, analogue of theophylline, compared with placebo, in patients with confirmed acute ischaemic stroke. Timing likely within one week (patients 'recovering from an acute ischaemic stroke').

Randomised, double-blind, cross-over trial of 250 mg caffeine versus placebo in 20 patients recovering from acute ischaemic stroke. Meets criteria: randomised, double-blind, analogue of theophylline, compared with placebo, in patients with confirmed acute ischaemic stroke.

Not a randomised controlled trial; no control group. Examines cerebral blood flow responses to aminophylline infusion in 12 patients but lacks randomisation and placebo/control comparison. Does not specify acute ischaemic stroke.
Animal study conducted in cats with experimental middle cerebral artery occlusion. Not a human trial.
Animal study in anesthetized dogs. Investigates cardiovascular effects, not acute ischaemic stroke in humans.

Appears to be a review or non-controlled clinical series (cites older literature, mentions 'controlled series are still lacking'). Not a randomised controlled trial, and does not specifically focus on acute ischaemic stroke.
